title: Response Playlet Brief Builder — inline incident fragment synthesizer for handoffs and rollouts
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Problem statement: On-call engineers and incident commanders need a fast way to assemble a lightweight, shareable ‘playlet’ during a shift change or active incident: a synthesized brief composed from alert fragments, SLO deltas, recent rollout state, and a short sequence of recommended next actions. Current handoffs are long, inconsistent, and require manual copy/paste from multiple console surfaces (alerts, traces, rollout history, cost view).

Goal: Design an inline composer inside the Redwood Console that can auto-generate a Response Playlet by synthesizing selected alert cards and incident fragments, attaching a one-line SLO snapshot, estimated cost delta for mitigation steps (quick preview), and optional links to a draft postmortem or runbook. The playlet should be exportable as a short message, attachable to incidents, and storable as a reusable micro-playbook for future incidents.

Scope: UX/UI prototype for the composer surface, content synthesis affordances (what fields are included/omitted), compact SLO and cost previews, lightweight approval flow (owner/approver tags), and integration points with rollouts to surface active canary/AB state. Not in scope: backend synthesis engine implementation and final RBAC enforcement (handled by ENG backlog items).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A mocked prototype exists in Figma demonstrating: selecting up to 3 alert fragments, auto-population of title+summary, an editable action list, SLO delta snapshot, and a cost-delta preview.
2) UX shows two export formats: short message (single paragraph) and incident attachment (structured).
3) Composer supports tagging an owner and optional approver before ‘publish’.
4) Generated playlet includes a link to the most recent postmortem draft if one exists.
5) Frontend prototype validates in user testing with at least 6 on-call participants achieving task success (create+publish playlet) in under 90s.
6) Design notes call out edge cases for suppressed alerts and partially-batched KV cache artifacts.
decisions:
- Use a single-line ‘SLO snapshot’ with three items: current SLI, 30m delta, and error budget impact.
- Cost preview will be a conservative estimate expressible in tokenized steps (e.g., scale-up GPU → ~$X/hr). We will show estimated delta range rather than exact cost to avoid false precision.
- Composer defaults to including top 2 alert fragments by recency but allows manual selection.
- Export formats will be a) plaintext message and b) structured JSON attachment for incidents; backend shape will be finalized with ENG-40221.
- We will surface rollout state when the alert maps to a recent rollout ID; otherwise hide that section to reduce noise.
next_steps:
1) Finalize microcopy for SLO and cost preview (Ava).
2) Run a 90s usability test with 6 participants — schedule with UX research (Rohit).
3) Prototype handoff to ENG with wireframes + API contract notes (target: ENG-40221).
4) Add product input on approvals and retention policy for saved playlets (PMs: Laila Chen).
5) Prepare design token handoff and interactive spec for console engineers.
